explanations: The IV in FieldCipher.encrypt comes from a hash of ticketId, so every encryption for the same ticket under the same key uses the same GCM nonce. create encrypts both the customer email and the body with that nonce, and every updateBody does it again. Reusing a GCM nonce leaks the XOR of the plaintexts (anyone who knows one value, such as a customer's email, can recover the matching bytes of the body) and lets an attacker work out the GHASH key and forge tags. The IV must be random (randomBytes(12)) for each encryption.

encrypt and decrypt both call setAAD with the ticketId. The value was sealed with T1 as AAD, and get decrypts it with row.id = T2, so decipher.final() throws on tag mismatch. The keyId is the same in both rows, and status plays no part in decryption.

KmsKeyProvider.getKey returns from this.cache before making any request, and the cache has no expiry, so keys already fetched stay usable. The 3-second timeout only applies when a key is not cached. There is a timeout, and there are no plaintext columns.

fetchKey uses node:https request with ca set to the KMS CA bundle. Certificate checking stays on (rejectUnauthorized defaults to true), so only a server presenting a certificate signed by that CA is accepted. Nothing turns verification off, and AAD is only used in the field cipher.
